editorial:
Imagine you are in a happy relationship, but suddenly you realize you might not be satisfying your partner. That is exactly what happens to Andy when he hears his girlfriend, Lauren, give a little sigh of disappointment after they are intimate. He totally panics and goes on a wild quest to become the best lover ever. Along the way, he gets some pretty weird advice from his buddies, professional porn stars, and even tantric experts. It is a lighthearted comedy that pokes fun at how men often overthink things in the bedroom while ignoring what their partners actually want. 

You will probably love the chemistry between the leads and the funny cameos from stars like Ken Jeong. While the plot is simple, the pacing keeps things moving quickly so you never get bored. It is not a deep masterpiece, but it is a great choice for a lazy Friday night. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you like keeping physical copies of your favorite comedies. It is a sweet, silly ride that reminds you that communication is way more important than any fancy trick you read in a book.
endingExplained: In the end, Andy stops obsessing over technical moves and fancy tips. He realizes that the physical side of things is not the real issue. He finally tells Lauren that he loves her, which opens up the emotional connection they were missing. Once they are honest about their feelings, their sex life naturally improves. They wrap things up as a stronger couple, proving that love and talking are the real secrets to a happy bedroom.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy rom-coms and stories about relationship mishaps.
